english.title: Member of a jury at an inquest share research with another member of the jury during the inquest period
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a member of a jury at an inquest, namely **(..IDENTIFY THE INQUEST DETAILS..), during the inquest period intentionally disclosed information, namely **(..SPECIFY INFORMATION DISCLOSED..), to

(A)_[another member]_
(B)_[other members]_

of the jury, namely **(..SPECIFY NAME(S) OF JUROR(S)..), having contravened paragraph 5A of Schedule 6 to the Coroners and Justice Act 2009 in the process of obtaining that information and that information not having been provided at the inquest
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 5B(1) and (3) of Schedule 6 to the Coroners and Justice Act 2009.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Information has been provided at the inquest if (and only if) it has been provided as part of evidence presented at the inquest, or as part of other information provided to the jury or a juror during the inquest period by, or with the permission of, the senior coroner dealing with the case.
